key_insight: The study provides the first direct experimental evidence of Kelvin-wave turbulence propagating along a single vortex filament, supporting weak-turbulence theory.
engineering_relevance: This demonstrates a measurable mechanism for energy transfer in vortex cores, relevant to understanding and modeling classical and quantum turbulent flows.
method: High-resolution spatiotemporal measurements of a single vortex filament
Spectral analysis of Kelvin-wave amplitudes across multiple scales
Comparison of observed cascades with weak-turbulence predictions
evidence_signal: The measured wave-amplitude spectra match the predicted weak-turbulence cascade and indicate six-wave resonant interactions as the transfer mechanism.
watch_item: The results are obtained under controlled single-vortex laboratory conditions, so extension to more complex turbulent flows may require further validation.
paper_title: Experimental evidence of Kelvin wave turbulence along a vortex core
